**Los Angeles vs. Berlin – Current Difference**

| City | Standard Time Zone | Daylight‑Saving Time Zone |
|------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| Los Angeles | Pacific Standard Time (PST) – UTC − 8 | Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) – UTC − 7 |
| Berlin      | Central European Time (CET) – UTC + 1 | Central European Summer Time (CEST) – UTC + 2 |

In **mid‑summer (e.g., May)** both locations observe daylight‑saving:

* **LA:** PDT (UTC − 7)
* **Berlin:** CEST (UTC + 2)

So Berlin is **9 hours ahead of Los Angeles**.

> Example  
> • When it’s 12:00 PM noon in Los Angeles → It’s 09:00 PM same day in Berlin.  

---

### Quick Reference Table

| Season | LA Offset | Berlin Offset | Δ Hours (Berlin − LA) |
|--------|------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| Winter (Nov → Mar) | UTC − 8 | UTC + 1 | +9 |
| Summer (Apr → Oct) | UTC − 7 | UTC + 2 | +9 |

*(Both offsets change at the usual DST transition dates.)*

If you’re planning calls or flights, remember this 9‑hour gap—just add 9 hours to your Los Angeles time to find out what time it is in Berlin right now!

So difference is 9 hours ahead: Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles. However, check whether there might be other variations due to DST transitions earlier or later. Usually DST starts second Sunday March; ends first Sunday November for US. For Europe, last Sunday March start, last Sunday October end. So as of mid-May, yes both are on DST.
